Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Judicial oversight exists but is not ID-specific. General constitutional rights, civil law remedies, and court access apply to ID-related disputes. The Digital Code provides for judicial notification by the APD in cases of criminal violations of data protection rules. Citizens can seek damages in court for data misuse. There is no dedicated ID tribunal or ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism identified.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Original sources (DLA Piper, dig.watch) describe the Digital Code and the data protection authority but do not directly address judicial oversight of ID matters. A supplementary source (droitnumerique.cd, updated May 2024, describing an August 2024 ministerial decree assigning APD functions to ARPTIC) confirms that the data protection authority's investigatory powers operate 'without prejudice to any action before the courts', supporting general, non-ID-specific judicial oversight. Value code 2 confirmed.
revised_comments: The judicial system provides general oversight of the digital identity and data protection framework in the Democratic Republic of Congo, but no ID-specific judicial mechanism exists. The Digital Code (Ordonnance-Loi N°23-010 of 13 March 2023) establishes a Data Protection Authority (Autorite de Protection des Donnees, APD), whose functions were assigned in August 2024 to the telecommunications and digital regulator (ARPTIC) pending the APD's own formal establishment. The authority's investigatory powers operate 'without prejudice to any action before the courts', confirming that individuals retain access to ordinary judicial remedies for ID-related data disputes, alongside general constitutional rights of access to justice. No dedicated ID tribunal or ID-specific judicial review mechanism has been identified.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Partial integration between civil registration and the national ID system. A June 2023 MOU between CENI, ONIP and INS aimed to transfer biometric voter enrollment data (45M+ records) to ONIP to underpin national ID issuance. However, the APAI-CRVS snapshot stated that DRC did not have a National Identity Management system in place, and the link between civil registration offices and identity management remains weak. Birth registration is required to obtain a national ID, but only ~40% of children under 5 have registered births (UNICEF data). The civil registration system has 979 local offices but no central repository.
revision_notes: Score revised from 2 (Partial integration) to 1 (No integration). The original sources (2023 MOU press report, a 2019 APAI-CRVS snapshot, and a 2025 NGO blog on birth registration) do not evidence actual system integration and partly predate the current state. A more authoritative and recent primary source - the DRC government's own April 2026 terms of reference for the national identification strategy (SNIP), published via mediacongo.net - explicitly states that the identification ecosystem remains fragmented and that civil registers, which are largely manual, are not integrated into any central file, with no interconnection to a single population registry. The February 2026 handover of the CENI electoral register to ONIP shows preparatory data transfer for the population file, not operational CRVS-ID integration. Revised down to reflect the absence of evidenced technical or systematic integration as of the latest evidence.
revised_comments: The identification ecosystem in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains fragmented, with civil registration, electoral, tax, health and population identification systems operating largely independently and without interconnection to a single population registry. A government terms-of-reference document for the national population identification system (SNIP), dated April 2026, states explicitly that civil registers - which are largely manual - are not integrated into any central file. Steps toward eventual integration are under way, including a June 2023 memorandum of understanding to transfer the electoral commission's (CENI) biometric voter enrolment data to the National Office for Population Identification (ONIP), and the February 2026 handover of the 2022-2023 electoral register to ONIP to help build the General Population File (Fichier General de la Population). The Family Code requires birth registration as a basis for identity documentation, but no operational data exchange between civil registries and a national or digital identification system has yet been established.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Digital ID-specific regulation exists. The Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 (Ordonnance-Loi) establishes a framework specifically for digital identity, electronic authentication, e-government (Guichet Numerique), and data protection. It creates institutional bodies including ANCE (Autorité Nationale de Certification Électronique) for trust services/digital certifications. The June 2025 PPP agreement with Trident for DRCPass also operates under this framework. Implementation decrees are still pending.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Digital Code N°23-010 (13 March 2023), verified via dig.watch and DLA Piper, establishes a digital-ID-specific regulatory framework (ANCE, ARN, ANC) distinct from general identification law, and remains the operative framework for the DRCPass rollout. Value code 2 confirmed.
revised_comments: Digital ID-specific regulation exists in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Digital Code (Ordonnance-Loi N°23-010 of 13 March 2023) establishes a legal framework for digital identity, electronic authentication, e-government (the Guichet Numerique one-stop platform) and data protection. It creates institutional bodies including the Autorite Nationale de Certification Electronique (ANCE) for trust services and digital certification, the digital market regulator (ARN) and the national cybersecurity agency (ANC). The subsequent public-private DRCPass digital identity programme, launched with Trident in June 2025, operates under this framework. Several implementing decrees remain outstanding.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: A data protection act exists. The Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 contains comprehensive data protection provisions (Book III) covering personal data definitions (including biometric data, fingerprints, iris scans), rights of data subjects (consent, confidentiality), obligations of controllers, breach notification, and penalties (USD 3,000-70,000). Previously, Law N°20/017 of 25 November 2020 on Telecommunications included initial data protection provisions. Several implementing decrees remain pending.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Digital Code's Book III (data protection), verified via DLA Piper, dig.watch, droitnumerique.cd and lexing.be, constitutes enacted data protection legislation. The dedicated Data Protection Authority (APD) was not yet operational as an independent body; its functions were delegated to the telecoms/digital regulator ARPTIC by ministerial decree of 17 August 2024. This does not affect the 'Yes' answer to whether the Act itself exists, so value code 2 is confirmed.
revised_comments: National data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the identity system. The Digital Code (Ordonnance-Loi N°23-010 of 13 March 2023) contains comprehensive data protection provisions in Book III, covering personal data (including biometric identifiers such as fingerprints, facial images and iris scans), data subject rights, controller obligations, breach notification and penalties. The dedicated Data Protection Authority (Autorite de Protection des Donnees) provided for under the Code had not been separately established by mid-2024; a ministerial decree of 17 August 2024 assigned its functions in the interim to the telecommunications and digital regulator, ARPTIC. An earlier Telecommunications and ICT Law (N°20/017 of 25 November 2020) contained the country's first, more limited data protection provisions.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The national ID card (carte d'identité nationale) issued by ONIP has legal proof status in DRC. It is the primary identity document for citizens. The voter card (issued by CENI) has also functioned as a de facto identity document for legal purposes. Under the Family Code (Law N°16/008, 2016) civil registration documents (birth certificates) are legally required for passports, education, and healthcare. The new DRCPass digital ID is designed to complement physical IDs as a verifiable digital credential for transactions. KYC regulations (BCC Instruction No. 15, AML Law) explicitly accept national ID cards as valid identity documents.
revision_notes: Flagged for human review. The cited sources (Smile ID, VoveID, ecoi.net) evidence that physical identity documents - principally the CENI voter's card, plus the passport and driver's licence - are accepted for KYC/AML purposes; none confirm that a 'digital ID credential' has legal proof-of-identity status codified in law, and the original comment's claim that ONIP already issues a national ID card with legal proof status is not supported. Fresh searches confirm that DRC's biometric national identity card (ONIP) had still not been issued as of mid-2026, with production and delivery repeatedly pushed back (officials stated in November 2025 and February 2026 that issuance was expected only 'next year'). The DRCPass digital ID (Trident/Tridentity, PPP signed June 2025) is in phased rollout but no statutory provision granting it legal proof-of-identity status has been identified. The evidence base does not clearly support a 'Yes' answer to this specific question about a digital credential's legal status; recommend human review rather than asserting a score.
revised_comments: The Democratic Republic of Congo has not yet issued a national identity credential from the National Office for Population Identification (ONIP) with confirmed legal proof-of-identity status; the long-promised biometric national identity card remained undelivered as of mid-2026, with officials indicating that production and issuance would begin only later in 2026. In the interim, the voter's card issued by the electoral commission (CENI) has functioned as the country's de facto sole national identity document since the country's last general identity card issuance in the 1980s, and is accepted for KYC/AML purposes alongside the passport and driving licence. A public-private digital identity platform, DRCPass (built on the Tridentity system under a June 2025 agreement with Trident), is being rolled out in phases for SIM registration, government service access and digital payments, but its formal legal status as proof of identity has not been established in publicly available legislation.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: A legal framework exists. Key legislation includes: Law N°20/017 of 25 November 2020 on Telecommunications and ICT (first data protection provisions); Digital Code N°23-010 of 13 March 2023 (comprehensive digital governance, data protection, cybersecurity, e-commerce, digital identity); Family Code Law N°16/008 of 2016 (civil registration); and KYC/AML Law N°04/016 of 2004 and Law N°22/068 of 2022. ONIP operates under the Ministry of Interior. The digital legal framework provides for national digital ID, electronic authentication, and data governance.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Multiple pieces of enacted legislation verified (Telecommunications Law 2020, Digital Code 2023, Family Code 2016, AML/KYC laws 2004/2022) via DLA Piper and dig.watch, plus a March 2022 decree (N°22/07) on the General Population File located via supplementary search (leganet.cd), which separately underpins ONIP's identification mandate. Value code 2 confirmed.
revised_comments: A legal framework governing digital identity exists in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Key legislation includes the Telecommunications and ICT Law (N°20/017 of 25 November 2020), which introduced the country's first data protection provisions; the Digital Code (Ordonnance-Loi N°23-010 of 13 March 2023), which comprehensively governs digital identity, electronic authentication, cybersecurity, e-commerce and data protection; the Family Code (Law N°16/008 of 2016), which governs civil registration; and anti-money-laundering/KYC legislation (Law N°04/016 of 2004, as amended, and Law N°22/068 of 2022). A separate decree of March 2022 (N°22/07) establishes the General Population File (Fichier General de la Population), maintained by the National Office for Population Identification (ONIP), which is tasked with producing identity and civil-status documents and assigning national identification numbers.
